did_you_know.text: The chapter opens by describing the people as “rebellious children”: they make plans without consulting the LORD and act independently of him.
Judah turns to Egypt for security and help, but the text emphasizes, “They did not ask me”—the decision was made without seeking the word of the LORD.

“An oracle concerning the beasts of the Negev” describes a dangerous journey through the wilderness, in which Judah’s messengers carry treasures on donkeys and camels to Egypt, a land of threatening animals.
The prophet calls Egypt “Rahab the Do-Nothing,” a name that, in context, expresses power that is useless and does not act on Judah’s behalf.
Isaiah is commanded to write the LORD’s rebuke on a tablet and in a book, so that it will be preserved as a testimony for future generations: “for the last day, as a witness forever.”
The people do not want to hear challenging prophecy. Instead, they demand that the seers and prophets speak “smooth things” and prophesy “illusions”—pleasant but deceptive words.
The consequences of relying on a crooked course are compared to a breach in a high wall: disaster will come suddenly, without prolonged warning.
The LORD presents the way of salvation in the words “in repentance and rest” and “in quietness and confidence,” but the people refuse it and prefer to rely on horses and flee on horseback.
When the people undergo spiritual renewal, they will receive clear guidance: a voice behind them will say, “This is the way; walk in it,” whether they turn to the right or to the left.
The future blessing is described as agricultural abundance: rain for the seed, bread from the produce of the land, spacious pastureland, and food for the animals.

The chapter paints a picture of healing and redemption: the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, the sun’s light will become much brighter, and the LORD will heal the wounds of his people.
Assyria, which the chapter mentions explicitly, will be shattered by the voice of the LORD and struck with his rod; this portrays divine judgment on the threatening empire.
